video_title: NEAR’s Plan to Make All of Crypto Feel Like One App
gist: Kendall Cole of Proximity Labs argues stablecoins will proliferate as unbranded ledger entries while issuer-backed chains mostly fail on credible neutrality, and that the real opportunity is chain abstraction: Near Intents now spans ~35 chains, monetizes 10-20 bps of swap volume routed to NEAR House of Stake buybacks, and is expanding into RWAs, euro stablecoins post-MiCA, and confidential (TEE-shard) trading. The host frames NEAR as the open-source financial super app, on the thesis that every successful crypto business model is ultimately an exchange.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole expects a large number of institutions to issue their own stablecoins, but as unbranded accounting entries rather than consumer brands, so USDC and USDT keep the branded-money franchise.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Bet on incumbents for stablecoin brand/network effects; treat new institutional stablecoins as back-end tokenized deposits rather than competitors for monetary premium.
insights.quote: I think what's going to actually happen is that a lot of different players are going to issue their own stablecoins, but they're not really going to promote them as an independent brand.

insights.claim: The framing both speakers converge on is that most future stablecoins are not money but ledger primitives: 'an asset in a ledger' used as a database entry inside an institution's stack.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole and host David
insights.so_what: Value accrues to the few liquidity/brand winners plus the rails that route between the long tail, not to each new issuer's token.
insights.quote: It's an asset in a ledger, yeah.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole flags OUSD from Open Standard (the Bridge crew) as an interesting new entrant attacking the branded-stablecoin market, but doubts it will make sense for users.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Skepticism on new branded stablecoin launches penetrating the USDC/USDT duopoly is a fade signal on issuer-token narratives.
insights.quote: we might see some like OUSD is kind of an interesting initiative, you know, from from the Bridge crew. Um but I I I don't think that's going to make sense for users.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole expects far fewer stablecoin-specific chains to succeed than stablecoins themselves, because the winning positioning for a chain is credible neutrality and issuer-backed chains structurally cannot offer it.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Underwrite Tempo/Arc-type chains on distribution alone and discount the rest; default routing likely stays with Solana and major L2s.
insights.quote: the best positioning for chains I think is credible neutrality

insights.claim: Kendall Cole's causal claim is that an issuer's own economic interest and value-accrual mechanism, while initially a distribution advantage, later blocks that chain from working with all counterparties.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Watch for issuer chains stalling after their captive volume is onboarded; the ceiling is the issuer's own franchise.
insights.quote: if you're backed by an issuer you have like way too much of an entrance interest

insights.claim: Plasma is characterized as following NEAR's pattern of building a blockchain designed to serve one very specific product, which Kendall Cole treats as a more viable model than generic issuer chains.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Product-first chains are a distinguishable subcategory from issuer-first chains when sizing new L1 bets.

themes.theme: Chain abstraction as Near Intents' product

insights.claim: Near Intents currently connects roughly 35 chains with new ones added weekly, positioning it as an aggregation layer where users think in assets rather than chains.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Chain count and integration cadence are the tangible moat metric to track for NEAR's aggregation thesis.
insights.quote: connecting I think 35 different chains and there's there's new ones every week at this point

insights.claim: The stated product goal has escalated from making users forget which chain they are on to making them forget chains exist at all, targeting a Robinhood-like brokerage feel rather than a crypto UX.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: The competitive set for NEAR's front end is brokerages and neobanks, not other L1 wallets.
insights.quote: initially the goal was to make it so you forgot which chain you were on, but increasingly the goal is to make it forget that you're on chains at all

insights.claim: Near Intents started as pure B2B infrastructure for wallets and aggregators such as Trust Wallet, Ledger and Li.Fi, and most of its volume still comes from those B2B2C partners rather than near.com.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: NEAR's revenue is partner-order-flow dependent, so partner churn or in-housing is the key downside risk, not retail app growth.
insights.quote: most of the volume for Near Intents still comes from all of these uh excellent partners that are more like, you know, B2B2C

insights.claim: The company's growth sequence was explicitly staged: integrate chains, then recruit solvers and market makers for quoting liquidity, then win integrators bringing order flow, and only now asset coverage as the main frontier.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A reusable bootstrap sequence for any routing/liquidity network; asset coverage is the current bottleneck to watch.
insights.quote: we're kind of coming out of that that like very long period of just like basically bootstrapping all of the chain integrations and all of the you know, like the liquidity

insights.claim: Near Intents is described as more than swaps: a NEAR account can custody assets on any chain and sign transactions to interact with any protocol on any chain, making swaps a background step.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: If chain signatures generalize beyond swaps, NEAR's addressable fee base extends to any cross-chain app interaction, not just trade volume.
insights.quote: the most important piece of of technology that was built there is account that can just actually sign any transaction on any chain

insights.claim: NEAR chain signatures only need to support EDDSA and ECDSA to cover essentially every chain that exists today, so new chain launches are close to zero marginal integration risk on the signing layer.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Low marginal cost per new chain means NEAR benefits from continued chain proliferation instead of being harmed by it.
insights.quote: there's really only two that anybody uses at this point and EDDSA and ECDSA. It's not a problem.

insights.claim: Gas abstraction on near.com means users only ever pay an explicit gas fee at deposit time from their origin chain, and never afterwards inside the app.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Removing per-transaction gas friction is the specific UX wedge that lets a crypto app compete with a brokerage app.
insights.quote: it doesn't feel like you as a user on near.com ever are touching gas fees

insights.claim: Because of chain abstraction, NEAR no longer needs to convince app developers to build natively on NEAR; developers can build anywhere and NEAR still intermediates the user.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Inverts the standard L1 valuation lens: judge NEAR on routed volume and partner integrations, not on native TVL or developer count.
insights.quote: we no longer have to worry about like getting convincing all of these different like great app developers to actually come and build directly on NEAR

insights.claim: The host reports Infinex uses Near Intents as the back end that lets him abandon a hardware Ledger for a password-manager login while still holding all assets, and separately consolidated dust from roughly 30 old wallets across Monad and Ethereum into near.com because it connects to every chain.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Real-world evidence that NEAR's distribution comes through embedded partners rather than brand pull, a pattern to track for other invisible-infrastructure plays.

themes.theme: RWA explosion as the next integration land grab

insights.claim: The host argues tokenized real-world assets are a far bigger opportunity for NEAR than meme coins were, because meme coins were inert and fleeting and nobody needed to integrate them, whereas RWAs create genuine cross-chain demand.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Routing infrastructure monetizes assets people must move between venues, so RWA growth is a more durable volume driver than memecoin cycles.

insights.claim: Robinhood chain launched on July 1st with roughly 30 tokenized assets including Nvidia, Tesla, Micron and AMD tokens, each with only about $400 to $1 million of day-one liquidity.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Tokenized equity liquidity is still trivially thin, so the near-term trade is the routing layer and liquidity provision, not the tokens themselves.
insights.quote: these all have somewhere between 400 and a million dollars of liquidity in day one

insights.claim: Kendall Cole says Near Intents support for Robinhood's tokenized assets is only a matter of time because demand is clear, and frames every new chain with unique high-quality assets as an opportunity for the abstraction layer.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Watch for a Robinhood chain listing on Near Intents as a concrete catalyst for routed volume.
insights.quote: only a matter of time before before that support will be uh near intense because clearly there's going to be demand

insights.claim: Kendall Cole cites SEC-enabled regulated tokenized products plus Polymarket and Kalshi-style prediction markets as having created entirely new asset classes that reset the integration roadmap.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Prediction markets are being treated as a first-class asset class by infrastructure builders, a signal for allocation to that vertical.
insights.quote: things like Polymarket that are in you know, Calico that have created like entirely new asset classes that are extremely popular now

insights.claim: Kendall Cole expects at least a dozen entrenched, thriving ecosystems rather than the near-infinite L2 fragmentation of the past, naming Solana, Ethereum, Tron and Hyperliquid as ones with sticky demand.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A bounded oligopoly of ~12 ecosystems makes cross-chain abstraction a tractable business rather than an impossible one, and concentrates chain bets.
insights.quote: we might not see the insane fragmentation that we had of like a billion L2s

insights.claim: The unifying user demand Kendall Cole describes is doing Hyperliquid perps, Polymarket bets, Robinhood chain Tesla, Aave on Ethereum and Solana stablecoin payments from one interface, which requires the whole stack to feel like one application.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Defines the actual competitive surface for crypto super apps: breadth of venue access, not depth on one chain.
insights.quote: if you want to do all these different things, you need an experience that makes that as just just feel like one application

insights.claim: The host argues layer ones were the original financial super app and that the open-source super-app thesis is now being expressed by near.com, which can surface anything of interest because of intents.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Frames near.com as a direct competitor to Coinbase/Robinhood super-app ambitions with a non-custodial, permissionless asset shelf.

themes.theme: MiCA fallout and euro stablecoin on-ramps

insights.claim: Only about 210 of roughly 3,000 crypto firms operating in Europe secured MiCA authorization by the July 1st deadline, a roughly 7% clearance rate.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: A 7% pass rate implies a large addressable pool of displaced EU users and firms for compliant or non-custodial alternatives.
insights.quote: Only 210 crypto firms operating in Europe received their authorization by the July 1st deadline. That's out of like 3,000.

insights.claim: Binance failed to secure its MiCA license before the deadline and is currently unavailable to EU users despite being the number one exchange in the region, while Bybit migrated users to its MiCA entity but cannot offer perpetual swaps there.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A concrete demand vacuum in EU spot and perps that on-chain venues and MiCA-licensed exchanges can capture right now.
insights.quote: if you're you know an an EU user you you currently do not have access to to finance which is pretty massive given that they are the number one exchange

insights.claim: Kendall Cole treats the combined Binance and Bybit disruption as a major tailwind for on-chain venues because previously friction-averse users suddenly need a new home.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Watch EU-origin on-chain volume and DEX/perp DEX share in the months after July 1st as the measurable expression of this shift.
insights.quote: that was like a massive sort of you know tailwind for the on chain space

insights.claim: Near Intents' core protocol is non-custodial, which Kendall Cole says means MiCA does not specifically apply to it, while integrators must run their own legal analysis based largely on how keys are managed.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Non-custodial architecture is being used as a regulatory-perimeter strategy; the compliance burden shifts to front ends and integrators.
insights.quote: NEAR intends, the core protocol, is in fact non-custodial

insights.claim: Monerium's regulated euro stablecoin EURe was launched on Near Intents and near.com the prior week, chosen early because Monerium gives European bank account holders SEPA Instant transfers into one-to-one, no-fee EURe on both on and off ramps.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A working euro on-ramp into a multi-chain asset shelf is the practical workaround to the EU exchange gap; track EURe volumes as the proxy.
insights.quote: Monerium gives them one-to-one no fees EUR E as basically in return for that for that euro and they do that for both on and off ramps

insights.claim: Kendall Cole names Gnosis as an especially good euro on-ramp app where a KYC'd European can bank-transfer euros and receive EURe on Gnosis chain with no gas fees, which can then be deposited into near.com.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Identifies Gnosis as a beneficiary of the MiCA-era euro on-ramp flow, an under-covered angle relative to headline stablecoin names.
insights.quote: Gnosis has done a very good job of creating an app that's like I mean incredibly seamless no gas fees all of that.

insights.claim: Solvers quoting EURe tightly against USDC as the underlying pair is what unlocks competitive euro-to-Bitcoin, euro-to-Zcash pricing on near.com, meaning routing quality rather than direct euro liquidity determines the user's price.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Solver competition is the real pricing engine; a fiat pair needs only one deep bridge asset to become tradable against everything.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole holds up Cash App's stablecoin integration, where users move USDC from a dollar balance without touching blockchains, gas or pricing, as the gold standard on-ramp experience that European banks should replicate.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: When banks absorb the on-ramp, the fee pool migrates from exchanges to routing and asset layers; watch bank stablecoin integrations as the trigger.
insights.quote: if we see that same experience moving to European banks, then it won't feel like an on-ramp anymore

insights.claim: The host argues MiCA's monetary-sovereignty goal backfires: thin, single-purpose compliant on-ramps like Monerium make it trivially easy to get euros on chain and then swap into dollars, so the regulation's walls are permeated rather than enforced.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Compliance-at-the-edge plus permissionless settlement is a repeatable pattern for regulatory arbitrage; expect more single-purpose licensed on-ramps.
insights.quote: All of a sudden like Mika regulations just don't matter.

insights.claim: The host states MiCA imposes an explicit daily transaction cap of one million euros of payment value on non-EU-denominated stablecoins used as a means of exchange within the EU, which he cites as a main reason large fintechs exited.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: If the cap binds, dollar-stablecoin payment volume in the EU gets pushed on-chain or offshore rather than eliminated.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole argues currency-control-style rules cannot beat market forces, but concedes MiCA has a genuine benefit in forcing every currency that wants global relevance to be tokenized, otherwise Europeans get shut out of the emergent frictionless global financial system.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Non-USD tokenized currency is a growth category regardless of regulator intent; euro stablecoin issuance should compound.
insights.quote: anything that's like looks or resembles kind of currency controls in in this day and age is not going to it good luck, you know, kind of escaping the forces of the broader market

insights.claim: Kendall Cole frames the GENIUS Act as strengthening rather than weakening dollar dominance, because stablecoins let the internet be denominated in dollars and stem any decline in dollar share.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Supports a structurally long view on dollar-stablecoin supply growth and on issuers levered to it, and suggests GENIUS is the better template than MiCA.
insights.quote: any declining dollar dominance is going to be stemmed by the fact that like people want to denominate the internet in the dollar

themes.theme: Confidential intents and the enterprise privacy bid

insights.claim: NEAR shipped broad confidential intents support to Near Intents partners on July 7th after roughly two months live on near.com only, extending private custody and trading beyond the first-party app.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A dated product catalyst; partner rollout is when privacy volume can inflect beyond near.com's own users.
insights.quote: today being July 7th, uh there was the we we were able to push out uh broad support for um, to confidential intents

insights.claim: The confidential shard works by having a subset of NEAR validators run a parallel chain inside a trusted execution environment that prevents them from viewing balances or transactions, with deanonymization only via validator supermajority agreement under a court order or user-issued viewing keys.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: The compliance escape hatch is what makes the product enterprise-sellable, distinguishing it from pure cypherpunk privacy chains that institutions cannot touch.
insights.quote: They're running it within a trusted execution environment, which enforces a set of rules where these validators are not able to actually like view, um, much information about what users are doing.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole claims the resulting product is the broadest privacy offering in crypto by number of assets and number of chains, since users can custody any Near Intents asset confidentially and trade the vast majority within the shard.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: If accurate, NEAR is a levered play on the privacy narrative that most investors currently express through Zcash alone.
insights.quote: it's the broadest by number of assets and definitely number of chains kind of privacy product that exists in the space right now

insights.claim: Kendall Cole's non-obvious call is that the second wave of privacy demand comes from enterprises protecting sensitive commercial information, not from broader retail, since treasury rebalancing and customer payments are competitively exploitable when public.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Prices privacy infrastructure off B2B compliance budgets rather than retail speculation, a different and more durable revenue base.
insights.quote: the next wave is not like broader retail it's actually is like most of the the feature requests that you know that I think like the industry is hearing is actually coming more from enterprises

insights.claim: The host attributes Zcash's first big price bump to the Zashi (formerly Zcash, now Zodl) wallet integrating Near Intents, which let users deposit USDC on Solana, swap to Zcash and shield it in one flow.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: UX integrations, not protocol upgrades, drove a major token repricing here, a template for spotting the next asset with a distribution unlock.

insights.claim: With confidential intents the pre-shielding leg becomes private too, so a USDC-on-Solana to Zcash swap that was previously publicly visible can now occur entirely inside the confidential realm.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Closes the on-ramp leak that made shielded balances traceable, materially improving the practical anonymity set for privacy assets.

insights.claim: The host argues privacy is only real at scale because a small privacy-seeking population is itself identifying, so expanding confidentiality from the Zcash hub to the spokes increases net internet privacy.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Anonymity-set size is the metric that determines whether a privacy product is actually usable, and it scales with default-on integrations.
insights.quote: you don't really get privacy unless everything is private

themes.theme: AI data extraction and Near AI

insights.claim: The host argues Anthropic and OpenAI are structurally competitive with their own customers because customer prompts containing alpha get ingested and turned into competing products, citing Alex Karp's remarks and Dylan Field's complaint that Anthropic launched a design product shortly after Figma was a client.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: Platform risk for AI application companies is a real underwriting factor, and a bull case for privacy-preserving inference vendors.
insights.quote: They launched like Anthropic design the design product right afterwards.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole predicts the frontier labs are too consumed by model competition to exploit customer data commercially today, but will monetize their data treasure trove through competitive products once margins get squeezed.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Timing matters: the platform-cannibalization risk to AI startups intensifies as lab margins compress, not before.
insights.quote: they have this like complete treasure trove that they will first are using probably just to make the models better, but ultimately will use for like competitive products once they, you know, their margins get squeezed

insights.claim: Near AI's early users are enterprises blocked from hosted models by HIPAA-style compliance rules or competitive concerns, and it also serves as the backend letting Venice offer end-to-end private inference.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Confidential inference is being sold on compliance, an enterprise budget line, and Venice is the visible consumer expression of that stack.

insights.claim: Kendall Cole flags that OpenRouter's model hosters are largely unknown parties who could collect user information, a risk he doubts enterprises are accounting for when they route to whichever endpoint is fast and cheap.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Inference-routing marketplaces carry an under-priced data-leakage risk that verifiable private hosting can arbitrage.
insights.quote: they also like do have all these kind of like pretty unknown like hosters of the models

themes.theme: NEAR value capture and the everything-is-an-exchange thesis

insights.claim: Near Intents monetizes by taking a cut of every swap routed through it, with near.com layering its own fee, averaging roughly 10 to 20 basis points depending on the partner and source of flow.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete take rate to model NEAR protocol revenue directly from routed volume.
insights.quote: the average is somewhere around like you know, 10 10 to 20 bips

insights.claim: Fees flow to the NEAR House of Stake, which controls the pool and has been buying back NEAR, so higher Near Intents volume translates into more buybacks or a larger token-holder-controlled treasury.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: A direct volume-to-token-value transmission mechanism; track routed volume and House of Stake buyback cadence as the NEAR valuation driver.
insights.quote: that goes into right now like the NEAR House of Stake, which basically controls that pool and has been at least quite a bit and buying back NEAR

insights.claim: Kendall Cole acknowledges the current monetization is limited to swaps and says there are many ways to monetize the infrastructure beyond that, with near.com used as a launch surface to capture revenue directly, as with the confidential intents rollout.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Optionality on non-swap revenue is unpriced today; new product launches landing on near.com first is the tell.

insights.claim: The host's organizing thesis is that every successful crypto business model is ultimately an exchange, tracing Ethereum, Uniswap, dYdX, GMX on Arbitrum, Hyperliquid, Lighter, stablecoin payments and even lending as forms of swap.
insights.speaker: host David
insights.so_what: A screening heuristic: value accrues where exchange happens, so evaluate crypto assets on volume routed and take rate rather than narrative.
insights.quote: any successful business model of crypto is doing some form of exchange

insights.claim: Kendall Cole endorses volume as the North Star for Near Intents exactly as it is for exchanges, accepting near-term trade-offs on take rate to win users and order flow.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Expect fee compression and rebate-style partner deals in the near term, so model volume growth ahead of margin.
insights.quote: exchanges make money by people exchanging

insights.claim: Kendall Cole expects AI agents to become a major new class of traders and to unlock an entirely new set of tradable assets, which he treats as future order flow for Near Intents.
insights.speaker: Kendall Cole
insights.so_what: Agent-driven order flow is an emerging demand source for chain-abstraction rails; watch for agent-native trading integrations.
insights.quote: agents will, you know, are and increasingly will be, you know, will be trading
